title: Bijectivity of normalized derived tensor-Hom maps
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, with the derived category of its modules and recorded derived tensor. Let $t_{K,L,M}:\operatorname{Hom}(K,R\mathcal Hom(L,M))\to\operatorname{Hom}(K\otimes^L L,M)$ be any family of functions satisfying the naturality and componentwise representative normalization of [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-model]. Then $t_{K,L,M}$ is bijective for every $K,L,M$.

source.place: Tag 08DJ (lemma-internal-hom); component calculation in sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 0A90

proof.text: Use the component-normalized tensor-Hom equivalence on homotopy classes. For K-flat P and L, Hom(L,I(M)) and I(M) are K-injective. Qh is bijective on maps to them. Conjugate these bijections by quotientCompQhIso, the internal-Hom model comparison, the inverse resolution map and the localized tensor model map. The latter is invertible by the upstream derived-monoidal K-flat criterion. For each chain representative the defining normalization of t and that of the homotopy equivalence give identical chain maps: equality on every total-tensor summand proves this by the coproduct universal property. Hence t on representatives is a composition of bijections. Choose K-flat representatives of K,L and a complex representative of M; naturality conjugates the arbitrary component of t by Hom-set equivalences induced by their isomorphisms. Bijectivity follows.
